cases.summary: "I have your password": recorded on webcam, pay $1,500 in bitcoin or the video goes to your contacts

input.visibleText: I hacked your webcam and recorded you. Pay $1,500 in bitcoin within 48 hours or I will send the video to all your contacts.

reasons.explanation: It threatens to send private videos or photos to people you know unless you pay. These emails are sent to millions of people, and the "recording" almost never exists. Don't pay and don't reply.
It mentions gift cards, wire transfers, or crypto. Scammers ask for these because the money can't be gotten back.
It asks for money AND rushes or threatens you. Together, these are a classic scam pattern. Check with the company or agency using a number you already have.
It tries to rush you. Real companies give you time to think.

cases.why: A blackmail threat. These emails are sent to millions; nobody recorded you.

cases.summary: Quotes an old password, threatens to share a recording with family

cases.summary: News: police warn about sextortion emails

input.visibleText: Police warn of a sextortion scam: criminals claim they recorded victims and threaten to send the video to their contacts unless they pay in bitcoin. Do not pay; report it.
